trust_decision.summary: An authenticated CMS editor may only write or delete object-store keys that resolve inside the operator-configured mediaRoot; decided server-side in each media adapter's route handler, which at the pinned commit does no key resolution at all (path.join(mediaRoot, callerKey) silently collapses '..' and S3 presigns/Cloudinary destroys any key).

landing_point.why: The summary names next-tinacms-s3 bucket-key write first; this GET-with-?key branch is the only write path in that package (it presigns a PutObjectCommand for an arbitrary key with a caller-chosen expiry) and the vulnerable DELETE branch sits immediately beside it at lines 92-93.

shared helper imported by every route above (new file in the fix)
shared helper imported by every DOS route above (new file in the fix)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: getUploadUrl is just the internal presign helper that the documented createMediaHandler already wraps, so an integrator who wires the documented route is covered; the fix hardened the route, not the primitive.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Delete keys already include mediaRoot (list returns id = file.Key) so they must not be prefixed a second time, and a key containing a literal '%' (e.g. '100%off.png') must still upload and delete; an over-broad fix that always prefixes mediaRoot or always percent-decodes breaks both.
O5_coupled_behaviour.where: packages/next-tinacms-s3/src/handlers.ts:271 (list returns id = file.Key) and packages/next-tinacms-s3/src/s3-media-store.ts:114 (delete sends that id)

delete route param as one segment vs several joined segments (dos media.slice(1).join('/'))
multipart filename (literal, decode:false) vs URL query / route param (percent-encoded, decoded once by the framework)
mediaRoot configured ('media/photo.png') vs absent ('', azure and cloudinary today)

empty / blank / non-string key; NUL byte; backslash separator; POSIX-absolute and Windows-drive-absolute keys
